clue.text: John Gilpin was such a man of the cloth

definitions.text: John Gilpin was such a man of the cloth

parts.words: John Gilpin was such a man of the cloth
parts.note: 'man of the cloth' usually means a priest, but here it is read literally as a man who sells cloth, which is the trade of Cowper's comic hero John Gilpin

explanation.surface: A remark that the hero of a famous comic ballad was a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: John Gilpin, the hero of William Cowper's 1782 comic ballad, is described there as a 'linen-draper bold'. 'Man of the cloth' wants to mean a clergyman; here it is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper who sells fabric and linen is literally a dealer in cloth.

clue.text: Ugly woman's into make-up as an aid to well-being

indicators.note: the ugly woman is placed into the make-up word, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: rouge is red cosmetic make-up for the cheeks
a hag is an ugly old woman; the 's means 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone suggests an unattractive woman should take up cosmetics to feel better.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'woman's' stands for 'is', joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Dietary fibre keeps the digestion regular and so helps general health.

clue.text: Irregular pressure put on workman

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece put on another sits above it, so the pressure letter comes first

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for pressure in physics
an artisan is a skilled manual worker

explanation.surface: Uneven pressure is being applied to a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irregular' looks like an adjective describing the pressure, but it is the definition, used as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An irregular is a guerrilla soldier outside the regular army, as is a resistance fighter.

clue.text: Mistakenly, let tiro go into opera

indicators.note: doing something mistakenly gets it wrong, so these letters are set out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: By error, a beginner is allowed to enter the opera house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mistakenly' rearranges LET TIRO GO; 'into' is a link word. A tiro is a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's work about the hunchbacked court jester is a famous Italian opera.

clue.text: Obtain post as head

parts.note: to land something, such as a job, is to obtain it
to post a letter is to send it

explanation.surface: Getting a job posted as head of an organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the westernmost point of mainland England, in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A head is a headland, a point of land jutting into the sea, and this Cornish one is the best known.

clue.text: Unorthodox 'approach not getting across in this case

definitions.text: Unorthodox 'approach not getting across in this case

parts.words: Unorthodox 'approach not getting across in this case
parts.note: the first two words describe creative, sideways problem solving; the rest jokes that the sideways word, meaning across, belongs to a down entry in this grid

explanation.surface: A creative method that fails to communicate its point.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer's first word means sideways, which in a grid would be across; but this light runs down, hence 'not getting across in this case'.
explanation.definitionFit: Solving problems by indirect, creative routes rather than step-by-step logic is a famous unconventional method.

clue.text: Let down, fed up and delayed

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word is read from bottom to top, so it runs backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning
something delayed is late

explanation.surface: Someone feeling disappointed, fed up and held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FED into DEF.
explanation.definitionFit: To let down a tyre or balloon is to release its air.

clue.text: Agent is my ears abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or all over the place, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A spy says that a foreign operative serves as their ears overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges IS MY EARS.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy sent on a mission is someone's representative.

clue.text: Disparage attractive girl draped round car

indicators.note: a garment draped round something encloses it, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: dish is slang for an attractive person
the Mini is a classic small British car

explanation.surface: A glamour model is posed across a car for a photo shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attractive girl' is old slang that the surface reads as a model posing; 'Disparage' is the definition, not part of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To belittle someone's achievements is to make them seem less.

clue.text: Correct initially wrong total

indicators.note: initially here means that the 'wrong' word stands first, ahead of the 'correct' word

parts.note: out means wrong, as in 'your sums are out'
right means correct

explanation.surface: Someone corrects a sum that was wrong at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' says the word for 'wrong' comes before the word for 'correct'.
explanation.definitionFit: An outright winner or ban is complete and absolute.

clue.text: Witness flyer's decoration hung round a tree

indicators.note: a decoration hung round something goes about it, so these letters enclose the other piece

parts.note: AFM is the Air Force Medal, awarded to airmen
a fir is a conifer

explanation.surface: An aviator's medal is seen hanging around a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' before 'tree' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To witness a statement, or affirm it, is to declare it true formally.

clue.text: Shoot hero, oddly involved in whodunnit

indicators.note: being involved in something means being inside it, so the odd letters go into the shoot word

parts.note: a tiller is a shoot growing from the base of a plant

indicators.note: oddly means the first, third and other odd letters are taken

explanation.surface: In a mystery novel, the detective shoots the hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes H and R from HERO; 'involved in' puts them inside TILLER, a botanical term for a side shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A murder mystery is a kind of suspense story.

clue.text: Not one jail has incarcerated a clergyman

indicators.note: to incarcerate is to lock up, so the jail word holds the other letter inside it
Not one means the letter standing for one is removed

parts.note: a prison is a jail
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Not a single prison has ever locked up a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not one' removes I from PRISON, leaving PRSON; 'has incarcerated' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish priest in the Church of England is a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Ruminant made much smaller creature run away

parts.note: an ant is a creature far smaller than a ruminant
to elope is to run away secretly to marry

explanation.surface: A grazing beast made a tiny creature flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazelle-like animal that chews the cud is a cud-chewer.

clue.text: Wealthy man's funny dog beginning to chase rodent

parts.note: Pluto is Mickey Mouse's dog in Disney cartoons

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the start of the next word is used

parts.note: a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A rich man's comical dog starts chasing a rat.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'man's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person whose power comes from riches is a member of the moneyed ruling class.

clue.text: Vessel needed sound indication of wind direction

indicators.note: sound tells us to take the word as it is heard, not as it is written

parts.note: a weathervane shows which way the wind blows

explanation.surface: A ship required a reliable weathervane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a blood vessel. 'needed' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A blood vessel carrying blood back to the heart.

clue.text: Communist guerilla coveting new image

indicators.note: giving a word a new image remodels it, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A revolutionary fighter craving a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new image' rearranges COVETING.
explanation.definitionFit: The Viet Cong were the Communist-led guerrilla force in South Vietnam during the Vietnam War.

clue.text: At home with salt water and fresh

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
the Solent is the strait of sea between the Isle of Wight and the English mainland

explanation.surface: Relaxing at home with sea water and fresh water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Solent is the channel of sea between the Isle of Wight and Hampshire on England's south coast. 'fresh' wants to be water, but it means cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh, of a person, means cheeky or impudent.

clue.text: Part of army thinks it's a fabrication

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of the army believes the story is made up.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the end of 'army' and the start of 'thinks'.
explanation.definitionFit: A story that is untrue or invented is a fiction.

clue.text: Malodorous alien in Greek city bearing letter for Greek

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the alien word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a metic was a resident foreigner in an ancient Greek city-state
phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A foul-smelling foreigner in Athens carries a letter for a Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: A metic in ancient Athens was a foreigner allowed to live there without citizenship; 'letter for Greek' is just one Greek alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mephitic air is foul and noxious, stinking like poisonous vapour.

clue.text: Peg, a measure of spirits, a student is not drinking

parts.note: a tee is the peg a golf ball sits on
a tot is a small measure of spirits
L is for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A list of drinks culminating in a student who abstains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abstains completely from alcohol is sober by principle.

clue.text: Delicate stockings (out of fashion) you may wear

indicators.note: what one wears goes around one, so the stockings word encloses the other piece

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings
thou is the old-fashioned form of you, hence the bracketed 'out of fashion'

explanation.surface: Fragile stockings that are no longer fashionable but you might still wear.
explanation.walkthrough: '(out of fashion)' tells you to use the archaic form of 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hothouse plant or child is pampered and fragile, used as an adjective.

clue.text: Something difficult to cope with in a small quantity

definitions.meaning: an unruly child or a troublesome task is one of these, more than one can manage
as much as you can hold in one hand, so not many

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from what fills one hand: a little, or all you can manage.

clue.text: Pointed where god appears next to city

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
NY is New York

explanation.surface: A remark on where a deity turns up beside a big city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where' and 'appears next to' simply join the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiky, like a rose stem, means covered in sharp points.

clue.text: They open out, to show a beginner

indicators.note: out signals the letters are laid out differently, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: People open up to reveal a novice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges THEY OPEN; 'to show' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice or new convert is someone just starting out.

clue.text: Following enemy, no retreat — it shouldn't occur again

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so all the pieces together are read in reverse order

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
a foe is an enemy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pursuing a foe without falling back, a unique event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' turns F FOE NO into the answer, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A unique event that is not expected to be repeated.

clue.text: Get one rattier, in a stew

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: being in a stew means being in a muddle, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone making a person even more irritable in a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a stew' rearranges RATTIER.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Get' means annoy, as in 'it really gets me'.

clue.text: I don't believe you manage

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of disbelief, like 'go on!' or 'come off it!'
to cope or get by, as in 'how are you managing?'

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to cope, and also serves as a scornful dismissal of an unlikely claim.

clue.text: Confront and drive back two different animals

indicators.note: driving back sends things in reverse, so the two animal words are read backwards together

parts.note: an elk is a large deer
a cat is a feline

explanation.surface: Facing up to an attacker and repelling two kinds of beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive back' reverses ELK CAT to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a problem or opponent is to face and deal with it.
